PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep layout state per chat by default
PullRequest.Body:

`sessions.experimental.layoutScope` now defaults to `chat`: in non-phone desktop Agents windows, each chat keeps its own editors, Editor/Details composition, bottom-panel visibility, and selected panel view.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9974

## Change

- The setting's registered default is now `chat` instead of `session-shared`. It has no separate `agentsWindow.default` or Agents window override, so this is the only default to change.
- The setting keeps `experiment: { mode: 'startup' }`, and explicit user settings still win, including `session-shared`.
- Invalid and unsupported values still fall back to `session-shared` behavior.
- `DESKTOP.md`, `LAYOUT.md`, and `LAYOUT_CONTROLLER.md` now name `chat` as the default, and `LAYOUT_CONTROLLER.md` no longer calls the base `B*` rules the default behavior.
- Tests: the registration test now pins `chat` as the default.

## How to test

1. Run this branch from sources, so no experiment assignment applies, and open the Agents window without `sessions.experimental.layoutScope` in your user settings.
2. In session A, show the bottom panel. Open session B and hide the panel there. Switching between A and B now shows the panel in A and hides it in B.
3. Set `"sessions.experimental.layoutScope": "session-shared"` and reload the window. Bottom-panel visibility is shared across sessions again.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/sessions/**/*.test.js'`: passed, 8160 passing, 28 pending, including the updated registration test.
- `npx eslint` on the two changed TypeScript files: passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: no errors in `src/vs/sessions`. Locally it reports 390 errors elsewhere, all from the `electron` package missing from this machine's install, in Electron and Node layers this change doesn't touch.
- Not tested manually in a running Agents window.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The default-to-enabled call path, same-session owner-key change, two whole-collection JSON serializations, and full editor-grid apply are directly established by the configuration, controller, and EditorParts implementations. Exact milliseconds vary with tab count and editor types, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and allocations from serializing all saved editor working sets twice, plus editor-group/DOM reconstruction for the incoming working set
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each switch among chats in one session costs O(total serialized state across visited chats) for delete/save persistence and O(open editor groups and tabs) for apply; the persisted collection grows with chats that have had editors open until those chats are deleted.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased chat-switch latency and UI/GC churn, especially in long-lived sessions with many chats or editor tabs.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With the previous `session-shared` default, changing chats inside the same session retained the session owner key, so it did not save or apply an editor working set and did not rebuild the editor grid. Per-chat behavior ran only for users explicitly opting in.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Making `chat` the registered default gives each chat a different owner key. On every same-session chat change, `ChatLayoutContext` invokes `_saveOutgoingWorkingSet`, and the target change invokes `_applyWorkingSet` for the incoming chat.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `default: 'chat'` at line 58 activates the per-chat owner/save/apply path for every desktop Agents window with no explicit setting; the deleted default limited that path to opt-in users.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding and serializing every editor working set on ordinary chat switches
Findings.Impact: For users without an explicit setting or experiment override, switching chats now synchronously snapshots the editor grid and rewrites the complete `editor.workingSets` payload twice (delete then add), then asynchronously disposes/recreates editor groups and restores the active editor. A session with many visited chats or tabs can therefore pause and churn the visible editor area on every chat switch.
Findings.Evidence: `BaseLayoutController`'s per-chat owner-change callback calls `_saveOutgoingWorkingSet`; `_saveWorkingSet` first calls `_deleteWorkingSet` and then `saveWorkingSet`. `EditorParts.deleteWorkingSet` and `saveWorkingSet` each call `saveWorkingSets()`, which JSON-stringifies the entire accumulated working-set array. The incoming path calls `EditorParts.applyWorkingSet`, whose `EditorPart.doApplyState` disposes all groups, deserializes the grid, and restores editors. The same-session switch does none of this when chat layout is disabled because its owner key remains the session resource.
Findings.Recommendation: Before changing the default, make working-set replacement atomic so delete+add produces one bounded persistence update, and add a same-state transition path that updates ownership without disposing/recreating the editor grid when the incoming chat's saved editor state matches the live state. Otherwise retain `session-shared` as the default.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a non-phone desktop Agents window with no explicit layoutScope value or experiment assignment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration lookup now selects `chat`; controller construction synchronously creates per-chat context and parses the persisted working-set, composition, pre-hide, visibility, and layout-state records before layout management is ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and JSON-parse persisted per-chat layout/composition records and editor working-set metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed number of records, each containing entries proportional to persisted chat owners; editor working-set state is proportional to saved tabs/groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With the old default these chat-specific records were not selected or registered for ordinary unspecified users; only explicit opt-in users paid this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation on controller startup; no subprocess, network, filesystem, or database request is newly issued because storage is already cached.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of persisted chats and the serialized editor/tab state retained for those chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, serialized startup initialization; no limiter or parallelism is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Storage values are read from the initialized in-process storage cache, then JSON-parsed into fresh maps. Cold profiles have no records; warm profiles parse all retained per-chat records.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: configuration selection and synchronous loading/parsing are direct. Exact startup duration is unmeasured.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persisted-chat and tab counts vary; startup parsing is linear but likely smaller than switch-time editor reconstruction for typical profiles.
Scenarios.Verdict: The added startup work is real but not separately reportable: it is one-time, cache-backed, and bounded by retained chat state with cleanup on chat/session deletion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch between chats of the same session while editor tabs are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The owner-change observer synchronously saves the outgoing working set before the switch settles. Incoming editor/detail composition waits for the serialized working-set apply/restore pipeline to settle, although the chat pane itself can change earlier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete the previous working-set handle and save its replacement; each operation JSON-stringifies the complete `editor.workingSets` collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full-collection serializations per switch when the outgoing chat has visible editors; collection size is one retained working set per chat with editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Under the previous session-shared default, same-session chat changes retained one session owner and performed zero working-set delete/save operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU and allocation in the owner-change event blocks switch processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose current editor groups, deserialize the incoming grid, recreate group views, and restore/show active editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized apply per effective owner change; DOM/editor work scales with current and incoming groups/tabs. Active editor restoration may resolve its underlying model according to editor type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same-session chat switches did not invoke `applyWorkingSet` with the old default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The chat itself can switch first, but visible editor and details composition remain in restore mode until this work completes, causing delayed layout settlement and UI churn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flush the latest workspace storage values to the storage process/database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Writes are coalesced in pending inserts, so repeated stores before flush normally become one IPC update per key, not two IPC calls per switch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same-session chat switches did not dirty these per-chat working-set/layout keys by default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the immediate switch critical path; eager JSON construction and in-memory update remain synchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is one outgoing and one incoming chat per switch. Save cost scales with all retained working sets across visited chats; apply cost scales with groups/tabs in the incoming and currently live editor grids.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Outgoing save is synchronous. Incoming applies are globally serialized by one `Sequencer`; rapid switches queue work, with stale-owner checks preventing some stale applies but not the synchronous outgoing snapshots already performed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Saved per-chat working sets are positive cached states. First visits miss and apply `empty`; revisits restore cached state. Storage writes update the in-memory cache and are coalesced for later flush, but JSON serialization occurs eagerly on each delete and add.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: tests assert per-chat save/apply calls, and production implementations prove whole-collection serialization and editor-grid reconstruction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual pause depends on retained chat/tab count and editor type; the O(total retained serialized state) double stringify and full grid rebuild are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: changing the default materially moves repeated whole-state persistence and editor reconstruction onto ordinary same-session chat switches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change side-pane composition or panel visibility, then delete chats/sessions or shut down
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visibility/composition changes synchronously update per-owner maps; composition writes serialize the complete map. Shutdown snapshots the active working set and serializes all retained layout entries before storage save completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize all per-owner composition entries on a layout change and all layout entries on shutdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per relevant UI change or shutdown; payload grows linearly with retained chat owners.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These per-chat records were maintained only for explicit chat-layout opt-ins; unspecified users used shared/session-level state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Composition serialization runs on the UI event path; shutdown serialization is on save-state handling. The eventual storage IPC is coalesced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chat owners with saved composition/layout state; cleanup cardinality is the number of peer chats owned by a deleted or archived session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous map mutation/JSON serialization; shutdown save is serialized. No concurrency burst exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-chat maps are warm in memory and persisted after changes. Chat deletion and session archive remove map and working-set entries, preventing unbounded retention for deleted owners; existing non-deleted chat history remains cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for linear synchronous serialization and cleanup ownership; low concern for magnitude because records are small.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Composition entries contain only small boolean state, and realistic retained chat counts are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: metadata serialization is linear but small, while deletion/archive cleanup bounds stale owners. Its heavier working-set counterpart is covered by the submitted finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use a startup phone Agents window or explicitly configure session-shared
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The presentation resolves to inactive/session-shared behavior, so per-chat working-set ownership does not activate.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: No changed per-chat multiplicity in this scenario.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged from the base session-shared controller behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat-specific records are not loaded through the enabled desktop-chat path; existing shared/session caches retain prior behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression for these configurations; they establish the boundary of the reported default-path impact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced startup, same-session chat switching, layout persistence/cleanup, storage flushing, editor-grid restoration, and inactive phone/explicit-session-shared paths. Submitted one medium-confidence-in-impact, very-high-confidence-in-mechanism finding for making repeated full working-set serialization and editor reconstruction the ordinary chat-switch path.
